crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Collections and payment plans in the AI Accountant covers the systems that manage overdue invoices, schedule customer payments, and decide when to escalate or offer revised terms. It spans invoice aging, dunning communications, installment proposals, promise-to-pay tracking, and the handoff to receivables staff or external collectors. The page also includes how these functions connect to credit control, cash application, and customer master data.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These tools typically run on top of an accounting or ERP system, drawing from open invoice tables, payment history, and customer contact records. They may use cloud services for sending email or SMS reminders and for hosting a self-service payment portal. Integration with payment processors and bank feeds lets the system confirm whether a promised payment actually arrived.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is usually a mix of deterministic rules and predictive scoring. Rules define when an invoice becomes overdue, which reminder template to send, and when a case moves to a collector. Machine learning models estimate the likelihood that a customer will pay within a given window, segment accounts by risk, and suggest a payment plan amount or duration that balances recovery with customer retention. Staff review and approve plans above set thresholds.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Collections systems sit inside consumer and commercial credit regulation, so the page tracks fair debt collection practice, data protection, and record keeping requirements. Rights and risk concerns include explainable scoring, audit trails for every automated message or plan offer, and the ability for a human to override a model decision. Provenance matters because a payment plan based on incorrect invoice or contact data can create a dispute or a regulatory breach.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more adaptive, real-time collections that adjust plans as new payments, disputes, or credit signals arrive. Expect tighter links to cash flow forecasting and working capital tools, so a proposed plan reflects its effect on liquidity. Voice and chat interfaces may handle routine negotiation, while human collectors focus on complex or sensitive accounts.
